sanskrit: nāśaṃsanta jayaṃ yuddhe dīnātmāno dhanaṃjaya ātmatrāṇe matiṃ kṛtvā prādravan kuravo yathā
english: No longer did they hope for victory in the battle, O Dhanaṃjaya; their spirits broken, the Kurus, fixing their minds only on saving themselves, fled away as best they could.

sanskrit: ke cid bhrāntai rathais tūrṇaṃ nihatapārṣṇiyantṛbhiḥ vipatākadhvajacchatraiḥ pārthivāḥ śīrṇakūbaraiḥ
english: Some of the princes were swiftly carried off in reeling chariots whose flank-guards and drivers had been slain, their banners, standards, and parasols gone, their chariot-poles shattered.

sanskrit: bhagnanīḍair ākulāśvair āruhyānye vicetasaḥ bhītāḥ pādair hayān ke cit tvarayantaḥ svayaṃ rathaiḥ yugacakrākṣabhagnaiś ca drutāḥ ke cid bhayāturāḥ
english: Others, out of their senses, mounted chariots with broken cabs and panic-stricken horses; some in their fear urged the horses on with their own feet from the cars; and others, frantic with terror, fled in chariots whose yokes, wheels, and axles were broken.

sanskrit: gajaskandheṣu saṃsyūtā nārācaiś calitāsanāḥ śarārtair vidrutair nāgair hṛtāḥ ke cid diśo daśa
english: Some, pinned to the necks of elephants by iron shafts, were dislodged from their seats; and some were borne off in the ten directions by maddened elephants that, tormented by arrows, ran wild.

sanskrit: viśastrakavacāś cānye vāhanebhyaḥ kṣitiṃ gatāḥ saṃchinnā nemiṣu gatā mṛditāś ca hayadvipaiḥ
english: Others, stripped of weapons and armor, fell from their mounts to the ground; some, cut to pieces, were caught beneath the wheel-rims, and others were trampled by horses and elephants.

sanskrit: krośantas tāta putreti palāyanto 'pare bhayāt nābhijānanti cānyonyaṃ kaśmalābhihataujasaḥ
english: Others fled in fear, crying out 'O father!' and 'O son!'; their vigor smitten by bewilderment, they no longer recognized one another.

sanskrit: putrān pitṝn sakhīn bhrātṝn samāropya dṛḍhakṣatān jalena kledayanty anye vimucya kavacāny api
english: Some, lifting up sons, fathers, friends, and brothers grievously wounded, loosened their armor and bathed their wounds with water.

sanskrit: avasthāṃ tādṛśīṃ prāpya hate droṇe drutaṃ balam punarāvartitaṃ kena yadi jānāsi śaṃsa me
english: Reduced to such a state, the army fled when Droṇa was slain; if you know by whom it was made to turn back again, tell me.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ heṣatāṃ śabdaḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca bṛṃhatām rathanemisvanaś cātra vimiśraḥ śrūyate mahān
english: The neighing of horses, the trumpeting of elephants, and the rumble of chariot-wheels, all mingled together, are heard there as a mighty din.

sanskrit: ete śabdā bhṛśaṃ tīvrāḥ pravṛttāḥ kurusāgare muhur muhur udīryantaḥ kampayanti hi māmakān
english: These exceedingly fierce sounds, rising up again and again over the ocean of the Kurus, make my people tremble.

sanskrit: ya eṣa tumulaḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate lomaharṣaṇaḥ sendrān apy eṣa lokāṃs trīn bhañjyād iti matir mama
english: This tumultuous, hair-raising sound that is heard could, I think, shatter the three worlds together with Indra himself.

sanskrit: manye vajradharasyaiṣa ninādo bhairavasvanaḥ droṇe hate kauravārthaṃ vyaktam abhyeti vāsavaḥ
english: I think this terrible roar is the thunder of the wielder of the vajra; surely, now that Droṇa is slain, Vāsava is coming for the sake of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭalomakūpāḥ sma saṃvignarathakuñjarāḥ dhanaṃjaya guruṃ śrutvā tatra nādaṃ subhīṣaṇam
english: The hairs of our bodies stood erect, and our chariot-warriors and elephants were thrown into panic, O Dhanaṃjaya, on hearing there that deep and most terrible roar.

sanskrit: ka eṣa kauravān dīrṇān avasthāpya mahārathaḥ nivartayati yuddhārthaṃ mṛdhe deveśvaro yathā
english: Who is this great chariot-warrior who, having rallied the broken Kauravas, turns them back to battle in the fray, like the lord of the gods himself?

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca udyamyātmānam ugrāya karmaṇe dhairyam āsthitāḥ dhamanti kauravāḥ śaṅkhān yasya vīryam upāśritāḥ
english: Arjuna said: Rousing themselves to a terrible deed and standing firm in resolve, the Kauravas blow their conches, relying on the valor of one man.

sanskrit: yatra te saṃśayo rājan nyastaśastre gurau hate dhārtarāṣṭrān avasthāpya ka eṣa nadatīti ha
english: The one about whom you are in doubt, O king—who, now that the teacher who had laid down his weapons is slain, has rallied the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and roars aloud—

sanskrit: hrīmantaṃ taṃ mahābāhuṃ mattadviradagāminam vyākhyāsyāmy ugrakarmāṇaṃ kurūṇām abhayaṃkaram
english: that modest one, mighty-armed, who moves with the gait of a rutting elephant, of terrible deeds, the giver of fearlessness to the Kurus—him I shall describe to you.

sanskrit: yasmiñ jāte dadau droṇo gavāṃ daśaśataṃ dhanam brāhmaṇebhyo mahārhebhyaḥ so 'śvatthāmaiṣa garjati
english: He at whose birth Droṇa gave a thousand cows in wealth to most worthy Brāhmaṇas—that one, Aśvatthāman, is the one who roars.

sanskrit: jātamātreṇa vīreṇa yenoccaiḥśravasā iva heṣatā kampitā bhūmir lokāś ca sakalās trayaḥ
english: By that hero, the moment he was born, neighing like Uccaiḥśravas, the earth and all three worlds were made to tremble.

sanskrit: tac chrutvāntarhitaṃ bhūtaṃ nāma cāsyākarot tadā aśvatthāmeti so 'dyaiṣa śūro nadati pāṇḍava
english: Hearing this, an unseen being then gave him his name—'Aśvatthāman'; and that hero it is who roars today, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yo 'dyānātha ivākramya pārṣatena hatas tathā karmaṇā sunṛśaṃsena tasya nātho vyavasthitaḥ
english: For him who today, as though he had no protector, was thus assailed and slain by the son of Pṛṣata through a most cruel deed, a protector now stands forth.

sanskrit: guruṃ me yatra pāñcālyaḥ keśapakṣe parāmṛśat tan na jātu kṣamed drauṇir jānan pauruṣam ātmanaḥ
english: That the prince of the Pāñcālas laid hold of my teacher by the locks of his hair—this the son of Droṇa, knowing his own manhood, will never forgive.

sanskrit: upacīrṇo gurur mithyā bhavatā rājyakāraṇāt dharmajñena satā nāma so 'dharmaḥ sumahān kṛtaḥ
english: By you the teacher was approached with a falsehood for the sake of the kingdom; though called a knower of righteousness, you have committed a most grievous unrighteousness.

sanskrit: sarvadharmopapanno 'yaṃ mama śiṣyaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ nāyaṃ vakṣyati mithyeti pratyayaṃ kṛtavāṃs tvayi
english: 'This Pāṇḍava is endowed with every virtue and is my pupil; he will not speak a falsehood'—such was the trust he placed in you.

sanskrit: sa satyakañcukaṃ nāma praviṣṭena tato 'nṛtam ācārya ukto bhavatā hataḥ kuñjara ity uta
english: And so, with the untruth clad in the garb of truth, he, the teacher, was told by you, 'The elephant is slain.'

sanskrit: tataḥ śastraṃ samutsṛjya nirmamo gatacetanaḥ āsīt sa vihvalo rājan yathā dṛṣṭas tvayā vibhuḥ
english: Then, casting away his weapons, freed of all attachment and bereft of his senses, that lord became overcome, O king, just as you saw him.

sanskrit: sa tu śokena cāviṣṭo vimukhaḥ putravatsalaḥ śāśvataṃ dharmam utsṛjya guruḥ śiṣyeṇa ghātitaḥ
english: Filled with grief and turned away from the fight, fond of his son—the teacher, abandoning the eternal law, was struck down by his own pupil.

sanskrit: nyastaśastram adharmeṇa ghātayitvā guruṃ bhavān rakṣatv idānīṃ sāmātyo yadi śaknoṣi pārṣatam
english: Having unrighteously caused the teacher to be slain when he had laid down his weapons, let your lordship now, with your counselors, protect the son of Pṛṣata if you can.

sanskrit: grastam ācāryaputreṇa kruddhena hatabandhunā sarve vayaṃ paritrātuṃ na śakṣyāmo 'dya pārṣatam
english: When the son of the teacher, enraged and bereft of his kinsman, has seized the son of Pṛṣata, not all of us together shall be able to save him today.

sanskrit: sauhārdaṃ sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ karoty atimātraśaḥ so 'dya keśagrahaṃ śrutvā pitur dhakṣyati no raṇe
english: He who shows boundless friendship toward all beings—when he hears today of his father being seized by the hair, he will burn us up in battle.

sanskrit: vikrośamāne hi mayi bhṛśam ācāryagṛddhini avakīrya svadharmaṃ hi śiṣyeṇa nihato guruḥ
english: Though I cried out aloud, longing eagerly for the teacher, yet the teacher was slain by his pupil, who cast aside his own duty.

sanskrit: yadā gataṃ vayo bhūyaḥ śiṣṭam alpataraṃ ca naḥ tasyedānīṃ vikāro 'yam adharmo yatkṛto mahān
english: When the greater part of his life had passed and but little of ours remains, this monstrous wrong was now done to him—a great unrighteousness.

sanskrit: piteva nityaṃ sauhārdāt piteva sa hi dharmataḥ so 'lpakālasya rājyasya kāraṇān nihato guruḥ
english: Ever like a father in his affection, and like a father indeed by right—that teacher was slain for the sake of a kingdom that lasts but a little while.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa bhīṣmāya droṇāya ca viśāṃ pate visṛṣṭā pṛthivī sarvā saha putraiś ca tatparaiḥ
english: By Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O lord of peoples, the whole earth, together with his sons devoted to them, was made over to Bhīṣma and to Droṇa.

sanskrit: sa prāpya tādṛśīṃ vṛttiṃ satkṛtaḥ satataṃ paraiḥ avṛṇīta sadā putrān mām evābhyadhikaṃ guruḥ
english: Yet though he had won such a station and was ever honored by our foes, the teacher always favored me, his pupil, above his own sons.

sanskrit: akṣīyamāṇo nyastāstras tvadvākyenāhave hataḥ na tv enaṃ yudhyamānaṃ vai hanyād api śatakratuḥ
english: Undiminished in strength, he laid down his weapons at your word and was slain in the fight; while he was fighting, not even the performer of a hundred sacrifices could have slain him.

sanskrit: tasyācāryasya vṛddhasya droho nityopakāriṇaḥ kṛto hy anāryair asmābhī rājyārthe laghubuddhibhiḥ
english: Against that aged teacher, our constant benefactor, this treachery was wrought by us ignoble men of petty understanding, for the sake of a kingdom.

sanskrit: putrān bhrātṝn pitṝn dārāñ jīvitaṃ caiva vāsaviḥ tyajet sarvaṃ mama premṇā jānāty etad dhi me guruḥ
english: The son of Vāsava would give up sons, brothers, fathers, wives, and life itself—everything—out of love for me; this my teacher knew well.

sanskrit: sa mayā rājyakāmena hanyamāno 'py upekṣitaḥ tasmād avākśirā rājan prāpto 'smi narakaṃ vibho
english: And yet, in my desire for a kingdom, I looked on heedless while he was being slain; therefore, O king, head bowed down, I have come, O lord, to hell.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ vṛddham ācāryaṃ nyastaśastraṃ yathā munim ghātayitvādya rājyārthe mṛtaṃ śreyo na jīvitam
english: Having today caused the slaying of a Brāhmaṇa, aged, a teacher, who had laid down his weapons like a sage—for the sake of a kingdom—death is better for me than life.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā nocus tatra mahārathāḥ apriyaṃ vā priyaṃ vāpi mahārāja dhanaṃjayam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing the words of Arjuna, the great chariot-warriors there spoke to Dhanaṃjaya nothing, O great king, whether pleasant or unpleasant.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahābāhur bhīmaseno 'bhyabhāṣata utsmayann iva kaunteyam arjunaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīmasena, enraged, as if smiling, addressed the son of Kuntī, Arjuna, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: munir yathāraṇyagato bhāṣase dharmasaṃhitam nyastadaṇḍo yathā pārtha brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: You speak words bound up with righteousness, O Pārtha, like a sage gone to the forest, like a Brāhmaṇa of strict vows who has laid down the rod of punishment.

sanskrit: kṣatāt trātā kṣatāj jīvan kṣāntas triṣv api sādhuṣu kṣatriyaḥ kṣitim āpnoti kṣipraṃ dharmaṃ yaśaḥ śriyam
english: A protector from harm, surviving harm, forbearing toward the good of all three orders—such a Kṣatriya swiftly wins the earth, righteousness, fame, and prosperity.

sanskrit: sa bhavān kṣatriyaguṇair yuktaḥ sarvaiḥ kulodvahaḥ avipaścid yathā vākyaṃ vyāharan nādya śobhase
english: You, the upholder of our line, endowed with all the virtues of a Kṣatriya, do not shine today, speaking your words like a man of no understanding.

sanskrit: parākramas te kaunteya śakrasyeva śacīpateḥ na cātivartase dharmaṃ velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: Your prowess, O son of Kuntī, is like that of Śakra, the lord of Śacī; and you do not overstep righteousness, as the great ocean does not overstep its shore.

sanskrit: na pūjayet tvā ko 'nvadya yat trayodaśavārṣikam amarṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā dharmam evābhikāṅkṣase
english: Who indeed would not honor you today, who—putting behind you the wrath of thirteen years—still desire righteousness alone?

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tāta manas te 'dya svadharmam anuvartate ānṛśaṃsye ca te diṣṭyā buddhiḥ satatam acyuta
english: By good fortune, dear one, your mind today follows your own duty; and by good fortune, O undiminished one, your understanding is ever bent on mercy.

sanskrit: yat tu dharmapravṛttasya hṛtaṃ rājyam adharmataḥ draupadī ca parāmṛṣṭā sabhām ānīya śatrubhiḥ
english: But that your kingdom, while you walked in righteousness, was unjustly taken away, and Draupadī was brought into the assembly hall and laid hold of by our foes,

sanskrit: vanaṃ pravrājitāś cāsma valkalājinavāsasaḥ anarhamāṇās taṃ bhāvaṃ trayodaśa samāḥ paraiḥ
english: and that we were driven into the forest, clad in bark and deerskin, made by our enemies to endure for thirteen years a state we did not deserve—

sanskrit: etāny amarṣasthānāni marṣitāni tvayānagha kṣatradharmaprasaktena sarvam etad anuṣṭhitam
english: all these occasions for wrath you have borne in patience, O sinless one; devoted to the law of the Kṣatriya, you have endured all this.

sanskrit: tam adharmam apākraṣṭum ārabdhaḥ sahitas tvayā sānubandhān haniṣyāmi kṣudrān rājyaharān aham
english: To undo that wrong I have set out, joined with you; together with their followers I shall slay those base men who seized the kingdom.

sanskrit: tvayā tu kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ yuddhāyābhyāgatā vayam ghaṭāmaś ca yathāśakti tvaṃ tu no 'dya jugupsase
english: It was said by you before that we had come for battle; and we strive with all our might—yet today you reproach us.

sanskrit: svadharmaṃ necchase jñātuṃ mithyā vacanam eva te bhayārditānām asmākaṃ vācā marmāṇi kṛntasi
english: You will not understand your own duty; your words are false. With your speech you cut to the quick of us who are stricken with fear.

sanskrit: vapan vraṇe kṣāram iva kṣatānāṃ śatrukarśana vidīryate me hṛdayaṃ tvayā vākśalyapīḍitam
english: Like one strewing caustic upon the wounds of the wounded, O scourge of foes, you make my heart split asunder, tormented by the arrow of your words.

sanskrit: adharmam etad vipulaṃ dhārmikaḥ san na budhyase yat tvam ātmānam asmāṃś ca praśaṃsyān na praśaṃsasi yaḥ kalāṃ ṣoḍaśīṃ tvatto nārhate taṃ praśaṃsasi
english: Righteous though you are, you do not perceive this monstrous wrong—that you praise neither yourself nor us, who are worthy of praise, while you praise one who is not worth a sixteenth part of you.

sanskrit: svayam evātmano vaktuṃ na yuktaṃ guṇasaṃstavam dārayeyaṃ mahīṃ krodhād vikireyaṃ ca parvatān
english: It is not fitting to proclaim one's own virtues with one's own mouth; yet in my wrath I could rend the earth and scatter the mountains.

sanskrit: āvidhya ca gadāṃ gurvīṃ bhīmāṃ kāñcanamālinīm giriprakāśān kṣitijān bhañjeyam anilo yathā
english: Whirling my heavy, terrible mace garlanded with gold, I could shatter the mountain-like beings born of earth, as the wind shatters trees.

sanskrit: sa tvam evaṃvidhaṃ jānan bhrātaraṃ māṃ nararṣabha droṇaputrād bhayaṃ kartuṃ nārhasy amitavikrama
english: You, then, knowing your brother to be of such a kind, O bull among men, ought not, O you of measureless prowess, to make us fear the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: atha vā tiṣṭha bībhatso saha sarvair nararṣabhaiḥ aham enaṃ gadāpāṇir jeṣyāmy eko mahāhave
english: Or else stand aside, O Bībhatsu, with all these bulls among men; mace in hand, I alone shall vanquish him in the great battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāñcālarājasya putraḥ pārtham athābravīt saṃkruddham iva nardantaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ hariḥ
english: Then the son of the king of the Pāñcālas spoke to Pārtha, as Hari spoke to Hiraṇyakaśipu roaring in his fury.

sanskrit: bībhatso viprakarmāṇi viditāni manīṣiṇām yājanādhyāpane dānaṃ tathā yajñapratigrahau
english: O Bībhatsu, the duties of a Brāhmaṇa are known to the wise: officiating at sacrifices and teaching, giving gifts, and the offering and receiving of sacrifices.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭham adhyayanaṃ nāma teṣāṃ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ hato droṇo mayā yat tat kiṃ māṃ pārtha vigarhase
english: The sixth is study; in which of these did the Droṇa stand whom I have slain, that you should blame me, O Pārtha?

sanskrit: apakrāntaḥ svadharmāc ca kṣatradharmam upāśritaḥ amānuṣeṇa hanty asmān astreṇa kṣudrakarmakṛt
english: Fallen away from his own duty and resorting to the duty of a Kṣatriya, that doer of base deeds slew us with a weapon not of human kind.

sanskrit: tathā māyāṃ prayuñjānam asahyaṃ brāhmaṇabruvam māyayaiva nihanyād yo na yuktaṃ pārtha tatra kim
english: He who employed magic, who was unbearable, a Brāhmaṇa only in name—if one slew him by magic itself, what is unfitting in that, O Pārtha?

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā mayā śaste yadi drauṇāyanī ruṣā kurute bhairavaṃ nādaṃ tatra kiṃ mama hīyate
english: If, now that he has been slain by me in that manner, the son of Droṇa in his rage makes a terrible roar, what is diminished in me thereby?

sanskrit: na cādbhutam idaṃ manye yad drauṇiḥ śuddhagarjayā ghātayiṣyati kauravyān paritrātum aśaknuvan
english: Nor do I think it any wonder that the son of Droṇa, with mere empty roaring, will get the Kauravas killed, being unable to save them.

sanskrit: yac ca māṃ dhārmiko bhūtvā bravīṣi gurughātinam tadartham aham utpannaḥ pāñcālyasya suto 'nalāt
english: And whereas you, becoming righteous, call me the slayer of a teacher—for that very purpose was I, the son of the Pāñcāla king, born from the fire.

sanskrit: yasya kāryam akāryaṃ vā yudhyataḥ syāt samaṃ raṇe taṃ kathaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūyāḥ kṣatriyaṃ vā dhanaṃjaya
english: He for whom, when he fights in battle, the proper deed and the improper are all the same—how could you call such a one a Brāhmaṇa, or even a Kṣatriya, O Dhanaṃjaya?

sanskrit: yo hy anastravido hanyād brahmāstraiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ sarvopāyair na sa kathaṃ vadhyaḥ puruṣasattama
english: He who, frenzied with wrath, would slay with the Brahmā-weapon men ignorant of weapons—how is such a one not to be slain by any means whatever, O best of men?

sanskrit: vidharmiṇaṃ dharmavidbhiḥ proktaṃ teṣāṃ viṣopamam jānan dharmārthatattvajñaḥ kim arjuna vigarhase
english: It is declared by those who know the law that, against violators of the law, what is like poison toward them is sanctioned; knowing this, O Arjuna, you who understand the truth of duty and meaning—why do you blame me?

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaḥ sa mayākramya ratha eva nipātitaḥ tan mābhinandyaṃ bībhatso kimarthaṃ nābhinandase
english: That cruel man, assailed by me, was struck down upon his very chariot; for this I deserve your praise, O Bībhatsu—why do you not rejoice?

sanskrit: kṛte raṇe kathaṃ pārtha jvalanārkaviṣopamam bhīmaṃ droṇaśiraśchede praśasyaṃ na praśaṃsasi
english: The battle being done, O Pārtha, why do you not praise as praiseworthy the dread cutting-off of Droṇa's head, like blazing fire, the sun, and poison?

sanskrit: yo 'sau mamaiva nānyasya bāndhavān yudhi jaghnivān chittvāpi tasya mūrdhānaṃ naivāsmi vigatajvaraḥ
english: He who slew in battle the kinsmen of me alone and of none other—even having severed his head, I am not yet rid of my fever.

sanskrit: tac ca me kṛntate marma yan na tasya śiro mayā niṣādaviṣaye kṣiptaṃ jayadrathaśiro yathā
english: And this cuts me to the quick—that his head was not flung by me into the country of the Niṣādas, as was the head of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: avadhaś cāpi śatrūṇām adharmaḥ śiṣyate 'rjuna kṣatriyasya hy ayaṃ dharmo hanyād dhanyeta vā punaḥ
english: To leave one's foes unslain, too, remains an unrighteousness, O Arjuna; for this is the law of the Kṣatriya—he should slay, or in turn be slain.

sanskrit: sa śatrur nihataḥ saṃkhye mayā dharmeṇa pāṇḍava yathā tvayā hataḥ śūro bhagadattaḥ pituḥ sakhā
english: That foe was slain by me in battle by righteous means, O Pāṇḍava, just as the hero Bhagadatta, your father's friend, was slain by you.

sanskrit: pitāmahaṃ raṇe hatvā manyase dharmam ātmanaḥ mayā śatrau hate kasmāt pāpe dharmaṃ na manyase
english: Having slain the grandsire in battle, you account it your righteousness; then when a wicked foe is slain by me, why do you not account it righteousness?

sanskrit: nānṛtaḥ pāṇḍavo jyeṣṭho nāhaṃ vādhārmiko 'rjuna śiṣyadhruṅ nihataḥ pāpo yudhyasva vijayas tava
english: The eldest Pāṇḍava is no liar, nor am I unrighteous, O Arjuna; the wicked betrayer of his teacher has been slain. Fight on—the victory is yours.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sāṅgā vedā yathānyāyaṃ yenādhītā mahātmanā yasmin sākṣād dhanurvedo hrīniṣedhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: He, the great soul by whom the Vedas with their ancillary sciences had been duly studied, in whom the science of archery was firmly established as in its very seat, restrained by modesty—
